title: Clean opportunity
summary: A well-specified managed security tender from a manufacturing group. Requirements are clear, the scope sits inside standard capability, and the open items are conditions rather than blockers.

insights.text: The customer runs two IT providers alongside each other and has no single party accountable for security across both. A single point of accountability is likely to matter more than any individual technical feature.
An earlier monitoring rollout at the group did not reach the coverage that was planned. Transition credibility will be examined closely.
Budget is committed for the initial term but described internally as tight. Price will need to be positioned as an investment against incident cost, not as a rate.
A prior assessment for a subsidiary means the organization is not a complete stranger. That is a foot in the door, not a relationship.

stakeholders.interest: Coverage across both providers, and evidence that alerts are actually acted on
A transition that does not disrupt production systems
A comparable, auditable price and a defensible award
Monitoring scope and what it means for staff

claims: Single supplier for the whole IT estate

Recruiting monitoring analysts in the customer's region.
Existing framework agreement with one of the incumbent providers.

comparison.takeaway: Depth is the difference. Their security practice sits inside a general IT business.
They are already in the building. We are not.
Own research and published findings versus a purchased feed.
Expect to be undercut on headline rate. Argue on incident cost.
